name: PCA9685 16-Channel PWM Driver
fullName: PCA9685 16-Channel 12-Bit I2C PWM Servo & LED Driver Board
tagline: Hardware 16-channel 12-bit PWM generator over I2C with zero microcontroller CPU overhead
description: The PCA9685 is an I2C-bus controlled 16-channel LED and servo driver. Each of the 16 outputs has its own 12-bit resolution (4096 steps) PWM controller operating at a configurable frequency from 24 Hz to 1526 Hz. It completely offloads timing-critical pulse generation from the main CPU, enabling smooth multi-servo robotic platforms (hexapods, quadrupeds, robotic arms).

specs.operatingVoltage: Logic: 3.3V–5V DC, Servo Bus: 5V–6V high current
specs.channels: 16 independent PWM outputs with 3-pin standard servo headers (Signal, V+, GND)
specs.interface: I2C (Default Address 0x40, configurable up to 0x7F with solder jumpers)
specs.frequency: 24 Hz to 1526 Hz (typical 50 Hz for analog/digital RC servos)
specs.protection: Reverse polarity protection on terminal power block, 1000uF capacitor slot

pinout.name: Output Enable
pinout.desc: Active-LOW global output disable (internally pulled down)

pinout.name: Servo Power
pinout.desc: Dedicated high-current 5V–6V battery / UBEC power for servos

wiringNote: Always power servos via the blue screw terminals with a dedicated 5V 3A+ power supply. Never draw servo power from the Arduino 5V pin.
libraryName: Adafruit PWM Servo Driver Library (by Adafruit)
commonMistakes: Supplying logic 5V to screw terminals without external battery (servos will twitch or reset MCU)
Forgetting common ground between external UBEC/battery and microcontroller
Setting PWM frequency too high (>60Hz) for standard analog hobby servos
